question: Under the Juniper merger agreement, what is the limit on Parent's obligation to take Remedy Actions to obtain antitrust approval?
key_facts: relative to the size of the Company
reference_answer: Parent need not take a Remedy Action that would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on Parent and the Company taken as a whole as a combined company, with the material adverse effect measured relative to the size of Juniper (the Company) and its Subsidiaries taken as a whole. That threshold is called a Burdensome Condition.

evidence.quote: provided, however, that neither Parent nor any of its Affiliates shall be required to propose, negotiate, commit to or effect any Remedy Action with respect to (A) any assets, categories of assets or portions of any business of Parent, the Company or any of their respective Subsidiaries if any such Remedy Action would, individually or in the aggregate, reasonably be expected to result in a material adverse effect on Parent and its Subsidiaries and the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole as a combined company (provided that for both of these purposes, a material adverse effect shall be measured relative to the size of the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, regardless of whether such actions are imposed on, or affect Parent, the Company or any of their respective Subsidiaries) (a “Burdensome Condition”)

question: How does the Juniper merger agreement define 'Superior Proposal'?
reference_answer: A bona fide written Acquisition Proposal that the Board determines in good faith, after consulting its financial advisor and outside counsel, would be more favorable to Juniper stockholders from a financial point of view than the Merger. For this definition the 20% threshold in Acquisition Proposal becomes 80%.

evidence.quote: “Superior Proposal” means a bona fide written Acquisition Proposal that the Board of Directors determines in good faith, after consultation with its financial advisor and outside legal counsel, taking into account the financial, legal, regulatory and other aspects of such proposal and any revisions to this Agreement made or offered in writing by Parent prior to the time of such determination, would be more favorable to the Company’s stockholders from a financial point of view than the Merger; provided that for purposes of the definition of “Superior Proposal,” the references to “20%” in the definition of Acquisition Proposal shall be deemed references to “80%.”
